holes_found.description: POISSON LOOSE-WINDOW NUMBER STILL NOT DEPLOYED (residual of c7 H0 / ISS-2702, closed via directional clause): detail_verdict_text now correctly notes 'any window drawn wide enough to include ~950 AD only raises this probability' but never quotes the actual loose-window range (P ≈ 0.70-0.91 on W=480, AD 900-1380, R∈[200,400], recomputed this run via Math.expm1(-W/R)). The reader is told the direction without the magnitude. A quantitatively careful defender can ask: 'if your point is that the loose window's P is higher, why won't you give the number?' The answer is that 0.70-0.91 is in fact the cited number's better-fitting cousin and the qualitative conclusion ('more probable than not') is unaffected — option (b) was a defensible minimal patch. But option (a) (recompute and deploy the loose-window range) would close the residual entirely. Severity remains minor because direction-only is sufficient for the argument; this is rhetorical polish, not a logical hole.
holes_found.recommendation: One-clause edit: replace 'computed on the historicist band; any window drawn wide enough to include ~950 AD only raises this probability' with 'computed on the historicist band; on a window wide enough to include ~950 AD, e.g. AD 900–1380, the same Poisson model gives ≈ 0.70–0.91'. This is the original option (a) from c7. Decider note: ISS-2702 was closed; if this is opened, file a small successor.

holes_found.description: FROOM REFERENCE STILL UNCHECKED AND DOING LOAD-BEARING WORK: detail_verdict_text says 'even granting only the four mainstream historicist anchor points (see, e.g., Froom, The Prophetic Faith of Our Fathers, vol. 2–4, 1948)'. Froom is print-only and citation_check has marked it unchecked across c6/c7. The four anchor dates themselves (AD 33 Resurrection, AD 313 Constantine, AD 325 Nicaea, AD 380 Theodosius) are basic Christian-history common knowledge that don't require a 1948 print citation. The Froom appeal is decorative and a defender can fairly pick at 'why are you citing a book you haven't read?'. Severity minor because the underlying anchor dates are correct (arithmetic re-verified this run) and a citation can be checked-or-removed without changing the argument.
holes_found.recommendation: Either (a) drop 'see, e.g., Froom...' and let the four anchor dates stand on their face, or (b) replace with a freely-verifiable source (e.g., the Wikipedia 'Historicism (Christian eschatology)' article or LeRoy Froom's article at the Adventist Encyclopedia). Both are one-clause edits. (a) is simpler and removes the unchecked-citation hygiene flag from citation_check.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome points at a real, peer-reviewed paleomagnetic result: the current SAA's reversed-flux patch dates to roughly AD 950 (wins.json WIN-023 detail_evidence cites Campuzano et al. 2019, doi:10.1016/j.epsl.2019.01.050, and Tarduno et al. 2015, doi:10.1038/ncomms8865 — both DOIs re-verified via doi.org handle API this run, responseCode 1). The arithmetic proximity of that date to the calendar millennium (50-year gap, 5% relative) is correct (wins.json WIN-023 detail_verdict_text, recomputed this run: (1000-950)/1000 = 0.05).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Pointing at a published measurement after publication is adoption, not prediction (wins.json WIN-023 code_analysis.post_hoc=true, re-validated this run); the dome's page states the match in one line with no derivation and no registration date (raw-text/02-wins.txt and live wins.html, both checked this run). The theological anchor is non-unique (wins.json WIN-023 detail_verdict_text's four historicist anchors spanning AD 1033-1380, anchor arithmetic re-verified this run), so the '5% miss' dissolves into either a clean miss of the rigorous band (83-yr gap from ~950 to AD 1033) or a base-rate-expected hit in a loose one (Poisson P≥0.70 on W=480, R∈[200,400], computed this run).

advocate_mode.best_defense: "The reviewers now have clean terminology and a sensible disjunction. But the case rests on saying the theological anchor is non-unique. ALL major Christian eschatological frameworks tie the millennium to a 1000-year span after some redemptive event. The dome's specific framing (full preterism) gives a target range of ~AD 1033–1070. Within that range, ~950 misses by 83–120 years — which the reviewers treat as a miss. But 83/1000 = 8.3% off a target the dome never tightly specified, and the dome's own page just says 'matches in full preterist timeline.' If 8.3% off a 1000-year span counts as 'miss,' then any millennial timeline claim is either trivially-failed or trivially-confirmed. The reviewers haven't given a principled tolerance — they've just chosen a band that makes us lose. Worse, they cite a 1948 Froom book they admit they haven't checked, while computing Poisson statistics to four decimal places. Their argument's strongest move (the 'wider window only raises P' clause) would require them to actually compute the wider-window number — they pointedly refuse."
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Two minor edits neutralize the live legs of this defense: (1) deploy the loose-window Poisson range explicitly (holes_found[0]) — kills the 'pointedly refuse to compute' bite; (2) drop or replace the Froom reference (holes_found[1]) — kills the 'cite a book you haven't read' bite. After those edits the defense collapses to '8.3% off a 1000-year span is impressive' — which the disjunction directly answers: rigorous reading => miss by 83+ years, no observable for the dome to claim a 50-year-precision tolerance; loose reading => the 50-year fit is in the base-rate-expected band (P ≥ 0.70 on any window wide enough to include 950). Optional bonus: deploy the AD 70 anchor (holes_found[2]) to make the rigorous-branch case self-contained from the dome's own framing.
